speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome to the clinic, I am Dr. Agent. To begin our investigation into your acute diarrhea, can you tell me exactly when your symptoms started and how many episodes of loose stools you have had per day?

speaker: Patient
text: 58-year-old female. The patient has been treated for community-acquired pneumonia with levofloxacin on the medical floor. She reports developing watery diarrhea with at least 9 episodes within the last two days, accompanied by lower abdominal discomfort and cramping.

speaker: Doctor
text: Based on your recent use of levofloxacin for pneumonia and the sudden onset of frequent watery diarrhea, are you experiencing any fever, severe abdominal pain, or signs of dehydration? Also, have you noticed any blood or mucus in your stool?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Watery diarrhea. I also have Lower abdominal discomfort, Abdominal cramping.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Antibiotic-Associated Diarrhea (Suspected *Clostridioides difficile* Infection).

Given your recent treatment with levofloxacin and the presence of frequent watery diarrhea with cramping, I am requesting a stool test for *C. difficile* toxins and a CBC to check for leukocytosis.

REQUEST TEST: Stool_C_diff_toxin_and_glutamate_dehydrogenase; CBC
